samples: This module turns a table (a header row plus any number of body rows of text) into a Markdown table string, padding every column to the width of its widest cell, header included, and adding a dashed divider line under the header. Rows that are shorter than the header are filled out with empty cells, but cells beyond the header's column count are silently dropped. It also includes a demo entry point that only needs console access and prints a small fruit-price table, so it's a lightweight, pure formatting helper with no file or network use.

This program turns a table, made of a header row and any number of body rows of text, into a Markdown table whose columns are padded to the width of the widest cell, header included. Missing cells in short rows are treated as empty, and the output includes the dashed divider line under the header. It is a pure formatting library with a `render` function you can call, plus a demo entry point that prints a small fruit-price table to the console, so it needs only console access and no files or network.

This program turns a table, given as a header row plus any number of body rows of text, into a Markdown table string in which every column is padded to the width of its longest cell (header included), with a dashed divider line under the header. Rows that are too short are filled with empty cells, so ragged input still renders. It is a pure formatting library with a demo `main` that prints a small fruit-price table to the console, and the only capability it needs is console output.

This program turns a table, made of a header row and any number of body rows of text, into a Markdown-formatted string where every column is padded to the width of its longest cell and a dashed divider line sits under the header. It exposes a table type, a function that computes column widths and a function that renders the table, plus a `main` that prints a sample fruit price table to the console. It is pure formatting with no file or network access, though rows shorter than the header are filled with blank cells, and cells in rows longer than the header are ignored.

It also includes a demo `main` that prints a small fruit-price table to the console, and it needs only console access, so it is safe to use as a pure formatting helper.
